newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL interbank rates softer on Bank Negara lending.
newsitem.headline: KL interbank rates softer on Bank Negara lending.

text.p: Interbank rates were softer on Tuesday morning as Bank Negara Malaysia continued to inject funds into the market, dealers said.
One-month money was at 8.0 percent against 8.3 percent on Monday, while the three-month rate was at 8.0/1 percent against 8.0/3 percent.
One-week money was steady at 7.9/8.3 percent.
"Negara is lending one-month money through an agent bank at 8.0 percent," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank. "It's trying to bring rates down gradually."

In a move to help control interest rates more effectively, Bank Negara announced on Sunday that local banks would have to limit their non-trade related currency swaps to $2.0 million with each overseas customer, from Monday.
On Friday, Bank Negara had asked banks to hold their base lending rates steady despite the recent surge in interbank rates.
The central bank has in the last two weeks been trying to lower interest rates in an effort to boost domestic economic activity.

Dealers said they heard that finance companies were being asked by Bank Negara not to bid in the market in order to keep rates down. In return, the firms can directly approach the central bank for funds, dealers said.
Finance companies are considered higher risk borrowers in the market and have to bid at higher rates.
No confirmation was available from Bank Negara, which does not normally comment on its open market operations.
Dealers said interbank rates might drop further on Friday due to maturity of Bank Negara bills worth one billion ringgit.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were mostly unchanged in thin early trade after posting sharp gains on Monday.
At 0315 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) September contract was unchanged at 92.40, or an implied yield of 7.60 percent.
